findings.text: follow-on: the fragment states 'five isolated runs that fail with scores 90', but the source it cites, state-probe-findings.md, records six (repro-1.log .. repro-6.log), and all six repro logs on disk carry 'scores 90' and fail; a committed evidence record undercounts its own cited probe.

follow-on: the probe logs the fragment leans on (repro-*.log, sha2-*.log) live only under /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261019T124040554227-a-stored-review-carries-its-total/, node-local scratch that dies with the allocation, while the fragment is committed to the repository; the durable record cites 36 runs of evidence that no later reader can open, and only state-probe-strace.log and state-probe-sha-scan.log were copied into the run directory.

follow-on: the manifest's tests and artifacts lines quote 'head 2 failed and 1037 passed' and 'head failures a strict subset of base', which no log supports and which its own armed after_suite object contradicts: after-suite.log at the reviewed head c5a07967e ends '3 failed, 1036 passed' with an added id absent from base and a base id dropped, so the strict-subset claim is false for the final arm and the quoted figures belong to the earlier ff2155a57 arm.

justifications.durability: the diff adds no assertion, only a fixture input change at tests/test_one_automatic_repair_round_per_run.py:151, and reverting it to six 15s would redden the unchanged '75' in reason assertion at :263 only when the fixture's random first-head sha lacks the substring 75, so the guard is probabilistic rather than a test that fails whenever the regression returns.
justifications.evidence: after-suite.log at the reviewed head ends '3 failed, 1036 passed ... EXIT=1' against baseline-suite.log '3 failed, 1036 passed ... EXIT=1' with one added id, and fresh-warm/fresh-1..5.log and warm-1..5.log each end '3 passed ... EXIT=0' (ten of ten), but the fragment undercounts its probe and the manifest quotes a stale 2-failed/1037-passed arm its own logs do not carry.
justifications.fit: tests/test_one_automatic_repair_round_per_run.py:141 carries a comment stating the mechanism, uses review_module.REVIEW_DIMENSIONS with zip(strict=True), and the fragment's new section follows the sibling-section idiom with no plan or ticket identifier in a name.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the gained commits land docs/evidence/fragments/every-review-is-kept-as-a-committed-record/a-stored-review-carries-its-total.html:26 and tests/test_one_automatic_repair_round_per_run.py:151, making the repair-round fixture's six scores sum to its recorded 75 so the derived total and the stored total agree, which is the §23 derivation reaching its last inconsistent consumer.
justifications.reuse: the diff adds no function, class or module, so no capability is forked; a search over tests/ and reckon/crew/ found no other owner of a stored-total fixture, and the fixture consumes the module constant it should.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff b3ea84199..81331dba4 changes exactly the two files the review names, and the repair-round test is outside the original five declared write paths but was added by the resume's scope grant, so both changes are authorised.
